article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Evening Brief
article.dek: Sunday's games are mostly in the books, Pickens sat and Ferguson went down hurt, and two games are left — here's what's still live tonight and tomorrow.

items.headline: Lead: Sunday is nearly done — the Giants stunned the Eagles, the Cowboys survived, and two games are left
paragraphs: Twelve of the fifteen Week 9 games are final. The Bengals beat the Falcons 34-17 in Madrid, the Giants beat the Eagles 19-11 for Philadelphia's seventh straight loss, and the Cowboys rallied past the Colts 27-23. The Chiefs rolled the Jets 35-12, the Lions beat the Dolphins 19-9, and the Saints edged the Browns 23-22 in overtime on Shedeur Sanders' first start.

Two games are left. The Buccaneers visit the Bears tonight at 8:20 p.m. ET, and the Bills visit the Vikings tomorrow night at 8:15 p.m. ET. Everything else is settled, so tonight and tomorrow are the only prices still live this week.
items.takeaway: Sunday's day games are final — Giants 19, Eagles 11; Cowboys 27, Colts 23; Chiefs 35, Jets 12 — with only the Bucs-Bears tonight and Bills-Vikings tomorrow left.

items.headline: Injuries: Pickens sat, Ferguson played and then went down, Henry played, Mahomes finished
paragraphs: The two Dallas names from this morning split. George Pickens was inactive with a hamstring injury — his first missed game since joining the Cowboys. Jake Ferguson was active, caught a touchdown in the second quarter, then hurt his left knee in the third quarter and did not return. He walked off under his own power, but the team has not said more yet, and Dallas hosts San Francisco next Sunday.

Patriots tight end Hunter Henry was active with his foot injury and played against Green Bay. And the scare of the day was Patrick Mahomes: a second-quarter sack torqued his throwing arm and he walked off holding it, but he came back on the next drive and finished with 242 yards and two touchdowns in the 35-12 win over the Jets.

Indianapolis lost two players for the game — linebacker Jaylon Carlies with a neck injury and right tackle Jalen Travis with a knee injury, both in the first half. Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward left with a hamstring injury in the third quarter but came back.
items.takeaway: Pickens sat with a hamstring injury; Ferguson played, scored, then left with a knee injury and did not return; Henry played and Mahomes finished after an arm scare.

items.headline: Weather: calm in Chicago, a dome in Minnesota — nothing to adjust for
paragraphs: The final forecast for tonight is calm. Chicago has wind at 10 mph with gusts to 17 mph, 53 degrees and a clear sky for the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. That is under the wind line, so it does not change how the game plays.
Monday night needs no forecast at all — the Bills and Vikings play indoors in Minneapolis. Nothing in the weather changes either of the two games left.
items.takeaway: Tonight in Chicago is calm — 10 mph wind, 53 degrees, clear — and Monday night is indoors, so weather is a non-factor.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so tonight and tomorrow still go through Check
paragraphs: Read again this evening, after the refresh, the board still shows Week 8, generated November 2. There are no Week 9 cards at all. It has not flipped, and it has not picked up any of Sunday's quarterback changes.

The quarterback fields are stale across the board. Philadelphia still lists Tanner McKee, but Joe Milton III started today. Cleveland still lists Deshaun Watson, but he was inactive and Shedeur Sanders started — and nearly won in overtime. Seattle still lists Sam Darnold, but he is out and Drew Lock started. Baltimore's quarterback field is still blank.

So there is still no Sunday night or Monday night card to read, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so tonight's and tomorrow's prices go through Check until the board flips.

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers — why 3 and 7 matter more than other numbers
paragraphs: In football, not every point is worth the same. Games end on 3 and 7 more than any other margins, because field goals are worth 3 and touchdowns are worth 7. A final score of 24-21, 20-17 or 17-14 is a 3-point game. A final of 27-20 or 24-17 is a 7-point game.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say a team is favored by 2.5 points. That is a very different bet from the same team favored by 3.5. At 2.5, a 3-point win covers. At 3.5, a 3-point win loses. One point of line moved the bet from a win to a loss, because 3 is the most common winning margin in football.

That is why you hear bettors pay attention when a line crosses 3 or 7. A move from -3 to -2.5 is a real improvement for the favorite's backers. A move from -7 to -6.5 is the same idea. The number itself did the work, not the team.
items.takeaway: Three and seven are the most common winning margins in football, so a line crossing one of them — like -3.5 to -2.5 — changes the bet more than a move anywhere else.

items.headline: The two games left both moved this week — the Bears got pricier and the Monday total kept falling
paragraphs: Chicago opened the week at -3.5 against Tampa Bay and now sits at -6, with the total at 47.5. The Bears are 6-2, the Bucs are 3-5, and the money kept coming for the home favorite all week. If your book still shows anything under -6, that is a better number than the market has now — run it through Check before kickoff at 8:20 p.m. ET.

Monday night moved the other way. The Bills-Vikings total opened at 46.5, fell to 44.0 during the week, and now sits at 43.5. The spread has not budged — Buffalo is still -3. A total that keeps falling without the spread moving usually means the market expects a lower-scoring game, not a different winner.

Sunday's finals landed against the morning's numbers too. The Giants covered -3 in their 19-11 win over the Eagles, the Chiefs-Jets total landed at 47 against a 48.5 line, the Madrid total landed at 51 against a 52.5 line, and the Lions-Dolphins total landed at 28 against a 49.5 line. The board has not picked up any of this yet, so run your book's price through Check — type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Bears -3.5 to -6, Monday total 46.5 to 43.5 — the two games left both moved this week, and the board has not caught up yet.

items.headline: Two games left — if Check says bet on your number, bet it now
paragraphs: Sunday night and Monday night are the last two prices of Week 9. If your book has a number you like on either game and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number tonight beats a hoped-for number tomorrow, because the Monday rush on a big-name team like Buffalo can push a line past the app's playable number just as easily as it can push it your way.

The only reason to wait is a real pending event. Monday's inactive list lands about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff — if your Monday bet depends on a player whose status is still open, that list is worth waiting for. Otherwise, the waiting is done.
A quick price reminder: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be.
items.takeaway: Run your book's Sunday night or Monday night price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now; wait only if your Monday bet depends on an inactive-list name.
